<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par150" />{{GHGpar-heading|150|Interrogative Sentences}}

H. G. Mitchell, ‘The omission of the interrogative particle,’ in {{GHGcite|title=Old Test. and Sem. Studies in memory of W. R. Harper}}, Chicago, 1907, i, 113 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|a}}
'''1.''' A question need not necessarily be introduced by a special interrogative pronoun or adverb. Frequently<ref>Mitchell (op. cit.) restricts the number of instances to 39, of which he attributes 12 (or 17) to corruption of the text. Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=24}} he would read, with the Samaritan, {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאַתָּה}} as in verse 21, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲשָׁלֹם}}, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲשָׁלוֹם}} as in verse 32; similarly he would read the interrogative particle in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=11|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=1|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=11|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=9|hidebook=1}}.</ref> the natural emphasis upon the words is of itself sufficient to indicate an interrogative sentence as such; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה זֶה בְּנִי עֵשָׂו|translate=thou art my son Esau?}} (but cf. note <sup>1</sup> below) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=פָּנַי י׳}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאוּל יִמְלֹךְ עָלֵ֫ינוּ|translate=Saul shall reign over us?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=29|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם לַנַּ֫עַר|translate=is it well with the young man?}} (but cf. note <sup>1</sup>); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=6}} (''should it also be marvellous in mine eyes?''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=16}}. So especially, when the interrogative clause is connected with a preceding sentence by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jn|chapter=4|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=וַֽאֲנִי לֹא אָחוּס|translate=and I should not have pity?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=22}} ''will they not stone us?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=11}}, 44<sup>19 ''b''</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=45|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=9|hidebook=1}}; or when (as in some of the examples just given) it is negative (with {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא|translate=nonne?}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=26}} (but cf. note <sup>1</sup>), {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=38}}.
<ref>But in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=27|verse=10}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} (which according to the usual explanation would expect a negative answer) read either {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מִי}} ({{GHGheb|text=עַל־מִי}}) with the LXX, or better, {{GHGheb|text=אָן}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָ֫נָה}}) ''whither?'' with the Targum. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=5}} read {{GHGheb|text=חֶפְצִי הֲלֹא}} with Wellhausen.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|b}}
Rem. The statement formerly made here that the interrogative particle is omitted especially before gutturals, cannot be maintained in view of Mitchell’s statistics (op. cit. p. 123 f.). The supposed considerations of euphony are quite disproved by the 118 cases in which {{GHGheb|text=הַ}} or {{GHGheb|text=הֶ}} occurs before a guttural.

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|c}}
'''2.''' As a rule, however, the simple question is introduced by ''He interrogative'' {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַ}}; as to its form, cf. {{GHGpar|100|k}}–{{GHGpar|100|n|nonumber=1}}), ''ne? num?'' the disjunctive question by {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} (''num? utrum?'') in the first clause, and {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}<ref>Quite exceptional is the use of the particle {{GHGheb|text=אִין|translate=num?}} (common in Aramaic) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=וְאִין יֶשׁ־פֹּה|translate=num est hic?}} The text is, however, undoubtedly corrupt; according to Wellhausen, ''Text der Bücher Sam.'', the LXX express the reading {{GHGheb|text=רְאֵה הֲיֵשׁ}}; but cf. the full discussion of the passage by König, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} xviii. 239 ff.—The above does not apply to interrogative sentences introduced by interrogative pronouns (§ 37) or by the interrogatives compounded with {{GHGheb|text=מָה|translate=what?}} such as {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּה|translate=how many?}} {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה|translate=why?}} (see {{GHGpar|102|k}}), {{GHGheb|text=מַדּוּעַ|translate=why?}} ({{GHGpar|99|e}}), or by {{GHGheb|text=אַיֵּה|translate=where?}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵיךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵיכָה|translate=how?}} (§ 148), &c. On the transformation of pronouns and adverbs into interrogative words by means of a prefixed {{GHGheb|text=אֵי}}, see the Lexicon.</ref> (also {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם}}, less frequently {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}}) ''an?'' in the second, e.g.<!-- continued on the next page --><section end="par150" /><noinclude>
